processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Alloy ingots with nominal composition Fe-35Mn-19Al-5Cu (at.%) produced by melting raw materials of high purity (>99.9 %) in a vacuum induction furnace under an argon atmosphere.
The ingots were homogenized at 1200 °C for 24 h.
Hot-rolled into plates with a thickness of 4 mm.
Plates cut into 10 × 5 × 2 mm3 samples using electrical discharge machining for Vickers hardness measurements and microstructure characterizations.
Samples solution treated at 1100 °C for 10 min under an argon atmosphere, followed by oil quenching (parent process proc_st-1100c-10min-oq).
Solution-treated samples aged at temperatures between 525 °C and 650 °C for 1, 3, 6 and 10 h, followed by water quenching; this sample corresponds to the 525 °C / 3 h condition.

structures.overall_structure: 19Al (Fe-35Mn-19Al-5Cu, at.%) low-density steel after solution treatment at 1100 °C/10 min and aging at 525 °C for 3 h. The microstructure remains essentially a single α (BCC) matrix; the α→β-Mn transformation of the 19Al alloy is very slow at 525 °C, so only a very small amount of β-Mn has formed. SE-SEM of this 525 °C/3 h condition shows a uniform α matrix with no visible precipitate at the 50 μm scale.

microstructure_list.region: bulk (α matrix with α grain boundaries)

phases_present.morphology: precipitates preferentially along α grain boundaries, with a minor amount of short rod-shaped particles within α grains; only a very small amount present at 525 °C for 3 h

precipitates.distribution: primarily along α grain boundaries; minor short rod-shaped particles within α grains

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Vickers microhardness measured using an HVS-1000 digital microhardness tester with a load of 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample tested 5 times and the hardness values given by the average of 5 measurements

hardness.region: solution-treated baseline (parent state of the 19Al alloy)

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Density measured by the Archimedes method

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Load 9.8 N, dwell 15 s; each sample tested 5 times and averaged
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure the Vickers hardness of the 19Al alloy in the solution-treated state and after aging at 525 °C for 3 h
characterization_methods.key_findings: Solution-treated 19Al = 263.8 ± 1.1 HV; after aging at 525 °C for 3 h = 574.1 ± 8.6 HV, a moderate increase reflecting slow β-Mn precipitation at this low aging temperature.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: ZEISS Sigma 300 SEM operated at 5 kV
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: SE imaging of electrolytically polished samples; 50 μm scale-bar fields with 10 μm insets in selected panels
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify the precipitation of secondary phases (α-Mn and β-Mn) in the 19Al alloy after different aging treatments (Fig. 9)
characterization_methods.key_findings: For the 19Al alloy at 525 °C/3 h the SE image shows a uniform α matrix with no visible precipitate at the 50 μm scale; β-Mn precipitation is very slow at 525 °C and only a small amount appears even after 10 h.

unmapped_findings: For this sample (19Al alloy aged at 525 °C for 3 h), the Vickers hardness is 574.1 ± 8.6 HV (Table 4), a moderate increase over the solution-treated baseline of 263.8 ± 1.1 HV; the aging hardening response of the 19Al alloy at 525 °C is gradual and fails to reach the alloy's peak hardness.

The α→β-Mn transformation of the 19Al alloy at 525 °C is very slow: the SE-SEM image at 525 °C/3 h shows a uniform α matrix with no visible precipitate, and only ~12.1 % β-Mn forms even after 525 °C/10 h (Fig. 6), the lowest among the three Al contents.
In the 19Al alloy aged at 525 °C the small amount of β-Mn that forms precipitates primarily along α grain boundaries, with a smaller amount of short rod-shaped β-Mn within the α grains.
The EDS-measured chemical composition of the 19Al alloy is Fe 41.6, Mn 34.8, Al 18.6 and Cu 5.0 at.% (Table 1).
